experiment: gbrain fix wave 9 mirror: search_path pinning insert cost (#5190) and the takes-quality protocol 2 comparability note (#5325)

source.release: v0.60.74.0 (PR title; VERSION at the mirrored head still reads 0.60.72.0 until the pending restamp)

search_path_insert_cost.change: every gbrain plpgsql function pins SET search_path = pg_catalog, public; the fact fingerprint SQL functions call pg_catalog-qualified built-ins instead, so they stay inlinable for the withdrawal index

measurement.kind: local timing on the wave lane's own machine, not a controlled benchmark
measurement.workload: insert 10,000 rows into facts through the withdrawal trigger

search_path_insert_cost.cause: the trigger function's pinned search_path setting (a function with a SET clause runs with a configuration change on every call)

correctness.evidence: test/fact-fingerprint-search-path.test.ts (PGLite) and test/e2e/fact-fingerprint-search-path-postgres.test.ts (Postgres) at the PR head: the golden was captured on master before the change; the index-plan case (EXPLAIN) passes on both sides

search_path_insert_cost.decision: about 10-13% slower bulk fact inserts (midpoints; range ends 6-16%) accepted as the price of security hardening; search results and fact fingerprints do not change

takes_quality_protocol_2.kind: protocol and comparability note, not a verdict
takes_quality_protocol_2.score_measurement_note: no before/after takes-quality score run was made; nothing here says protocol 2 raises or lowers scores
changes: one same-model correction per malformed judge slot (parse_failed, including an empty reply, or incomplete_scores), with the validator's error appended
each correction is priced against --budget-usd before it is sent; not sent means corrected null with skipped_reason budget or aborted
a corrected reply replaces the first attempt only when it validates (correction_selection_rule corrected_if_valid)
provider errors and valid low scores are never re-asked
correction calls count toward cost_usd and the budget cap
takes_quality_protocol_2.regress_behavior: gbrain eval takes-quality regress lists a protocol_version difference among the dissimilar inputs (inputs_differ true), as it does for corpus, prompt and rubric hash differences; it warns and does not refuse
takes_quality_protocol_2.comparability_rule: do not compare takes-quality receipts across protocol_version 1 and 2 as a like-for-like score change; report such a comparison as dissimilar inputs, and compare only receipts with the same protocol_version, model panel, corpus, prompt and rubric
